rule: The attribution cache is keyed by the full HEAD sha and the walk bound, derived only; any key mismatch or unreadable cache re-walks.
chose: For warm session-start (4.4's open <20 ms quiet-read bar), build L2 then L1, measure, and stop to report before L3 or L4 (approved by sofar-e8 within the operator's 4.4 scope, 2026-09-24). L2: the Rust core reads the digest, registration and guards caches with typed serde_json, with formats unchanged. It's a port-only cost, covered by the 2026-09-21 rule. L1: cache the bounded attribution walk per HEAD sha in a derived .sofar/.index file, TS first, then Rust, and output must be identical.
over: Starting with L3 (sharding the registration caches changes D35's format and needs its own Decision); restating the 20 ms bar before the exact levers are tried; a resident process (rejected)
because: The profile at team100 (53.5 ms relative): home_initiative 26%, digest parse 23%, the git attribution subprocess 21%, render_status 18%, guards parse 7%. A sha's ancestry is immutable, so a per-sha cache of the attribution walk is exact. Typed parsing is the D9-sanctioned fix for the core's slow generic JSON parser. The estimate is ~53 → ~22 ms after L1+L2.
